passages.text: This is the word of the LORD about the nations—the word that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Egypt and the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, which was defeated at Carchemish on the Euphrates River by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah: “Deploy your shields, small and large; advance for battle!
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet.
The LORD gave Jeremiah a message about the nations.
This message was about Egypt.
It was about the army of Pharaoh Neco, king of Egypt.
Pharaoh Neco’s army was at Carchemish, by the Euphrates River.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, defeated this army.
This happened in the fourth year of Jehoiakim.
Jehoiakim was the son of Josiah.
Jehoiakim was king of Judah.
The LORD said, “Prepare your shields, both small and large.
Get ready for battle.”
passages.original: אֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֧ה דְבַר־ יְהוָ֛ה אֶל־ יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא עַל־ הַגּוֹיִֽם׃ לְמִצְרַ֗יִם עַל־ חֵ֨יל פַּרְעֹ֤ה נְכוֹ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁר־ הָיָ֥ה עַל־ נְהַר־ פְּרָ֖ת בְּכַרְכְּמִ֑שׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִכָּ֗ה נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל בִּשְׁנַת֙ הָֽרְבִיעִ֔ית לִיהוֹיָקִ֥ים בֶּן־ יֹאשִׁיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃ עִרְכ֤וּ מָגֵן֙ וְצִנָּ֔ה וּגְשׁ֖וּ לַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

passages.text: Harness the horses; mount the steeds; take your positions with helmets on! Polish your spears; put on armor!
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Jeremiah the prophet.
God gave a message about Egypt and its army.
Pharaoh Neco was the king of Egypt.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, defeated Pharaoh Neco at Carchemish.
This happened by the Euphrates River.
This happened in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah.
God commanded the soldiers.
Harness the horses.
Mount the horses.
Take your positions.
Put on your helmets.
Polish your spears.
Put on your armor.
passages.original: אִסְר֣וּ הַסּוּסִ֗ים וַֽעֲלוּ֙ הַפָּ֣רָשִׁ֔ים וְהִֽתְיַצְּב֖וּ בְּכ֥וֹבָעִ֑ים מִרְקוּ֙ הָֽרְמָחִ֔ים לִבְשׁ֖וּ הַסִּרְיֹנֹֽת׃

passages.text: Why am I seeing this? They are terrified, they are retreating; their warriors are defeated, they flee in haste without looking back; terror is on every side!” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about Egypt and its army.
Pharaoh Neco was the king of Egypt.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, defeated Pharaoh Neco’s army at Carchemish on the Euphrates River.
This happened in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah.

I see them.
They are terrified.
They are retreating.
Their warriors are defeated.
They run away quickly.
They do not look back.
Terror surrounds them.
The LORD has declared this.
passages.original: מַדּ֣וּעַ רָאִ֗יתִי הֵ֣מָּה חַתִּים֮ נְסֹגִ֣ים אָחוֹר֒ וְגִבּוֹרֵיהֶ֣ם יֻכַּ֔תּוּ וּמָנ֥וֹס נָ֖סוּ וְלֹ֣א הִפְנ֑וּ מָג֥וֹר מִסָּבִ֖יב נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: “The swift cannot flee, and the warrior cannot escape! In the north by the River Euphrates they stumble and fall.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about a coming battle.
The swift man cannot run away.
The strong warrior cannot escape.
This happens in the north.
It happens by the River Euphrates.
They stumble there.
They fall there.
passages.original: אַל־ יָנ֣וּס הַקַּ֔ל וְאַל־ יִמָּלֵ֖ט הַגִּבּ֑וֹר צָפ֙וֹנָה֙ עַל־ יַ֣ד נְהַר־ פְּרָ֔ת כָּשְׁל֖וּ וְנָפָֽלוּ׃

passages.text: Who is this, rising like the Nile, like rivers whose waters churn?
passages.sermon:
Someone rises up.
This one rises like the Nile River.
His waters churn like rushing rivers.
passages.original: מִי־ זֶ֖ה כַּיְאֹ֣ר יַֽעֲלֶ֑ה כַּנְּהָר֕וֹת יִֽתְגָּעֲשׁ֖וּ מֵימָֽיו׃

passages.text: Egypt rises like the Nile, and its waters churn like rivers, boasting, ‘I will rise and cover the earth; I will destroy the cities and their people.’
passages.sermon:
Egypt is a powerful nation.
Egypt rises like the Nile River.
Egypt’s waters churn like mighty rivers.
Egypt boasts with pride.
Egypt says, “I will rise and cover the earth.”
Egypt says, “I will destroy the cities.”
Egypt says, “I will destroy the people who live in them.”
passages.original: מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ כַּיְאֹ֣ר יַֽעֲלֶ֔ה וְכַנְּהָר֖וֹת יִתְגֹּ֣עֲשׁוּ מָ֑יִם וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אַֽעֲלֶה֙ אֲכַסֶּה־ אֶ֔רֶץ אֹבִ֥ידָה עִ֖יר וְיֹ֥שְׁבֵי בָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Advance, O horses! Race furiously, O chariots! Let the warriors come forth— Cush and Put carrying their shields, men of Lydia drawing the bow.
passages.sermon:
Egypt prepares for battle.
Horses advance.
Chariots race forward with fury.
Warriors come out to fight.
Men from Cush and Put carry shields.
Men from Lydia draw their bows.
passages.original: עֲל֤וּ הַסּוּסִים֙ וְהִתְהֹלְל֣וּ הָרֶ֔כֶב וְיֵצְא֖וּ הַגִּבּוֹרִ֑ים כּ֤וּשׁ וּפוּט֙ תֹּפְשֵׂ֣י מָגֵ֔ן וְלוּדִ֕ים תֹּפְשֵׂ֖י דֹּ֥רְכֵי קָֽשֶׁת׃

passages.text: For that day belongs to the Lord GOD of Hosts, a day of vengeance against His foes. The sword will devour until it is satisfied, until it is quenched with their blood. For the Lord GOD of Hosts will hold a sacrifice in the land of the north by the River Euphrates.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts owns that day.
The Lord GOD of Hosts is the ruler of heaven’s armies.
That day is a day of vengeance.
The Lord GOD of Hosts will take vengeance against His enemies.
The sword will devour His foes.
The sword will eat until it is full.
The sword will drink blood until it is satisfied.
The Lord GOD of Hosts will hold a sacrifice.
This sacrifice will happen in the land of the north.
The sacrifice will be by the River Euphrates.
passages.original: וְֽהַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא לַאדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת י֤וֹם נְקָמָה֙ לְהִנָּקֵ֣ם מִצָּרָ֔יו וְאָכְלָ֥ה חֶ֙רֶב֙ וְשָׂ֣בְעָ֔ה וְרָוְתָ֖ה מִדָּמָ֑ם כִּ֣י זֶ֠בַח לַאדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת בְּאֶ֥רֶץ צָפ֖וֹן אֶל־ נְהַר־ פְּרָֽת׃

passages.text: Go up to Gilead for balm, O Virgin Daughter of Egypt! In vain you try many remedies, but for you there is no healing.
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks to Egypt.
Egypt is called the Virgin Daughter.
The Lord tells Egypt to go up to Gilead.
The Lord tells Egypt to take balm from Gilead.
Egypt tries many remedies.
Egypt tries to heal herself.
All her efforts are in vain.
There is no healing for Egypt.
passages.original: עֲלִ֤י גִלְעָד֙ וּקְחִ֣י צֳרִ֔י בְּתוּלַ֖ת בַּת־ מִצְרָ֑יִם לַשָּׁוְא֙ הִרְבֵּיתִי רְפֻא֔וֹת תְּעָלָ֖ה אֵ֥ין לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: The nations have heard of your shame, and your outcry fills the earth, because warrior stumbles over warrior and both of them have fallen together.”
passages.sermon:
The nations have heard about your shame.
Your outcry fills the whole earth.
One warrior stumbles over another warrior.
Both warriors have fallen together.
passages.original: שָׁמְע֤וּ גוֹיִם֙ קְלוֹנֵ֔ךְ וְצִוְחָתֵ֖ךְ מָלְאָ֣ה הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּֽי־ גִבּ֤וֹר בְּגִבּוֹר֙ כָּשָׁ֔לוּ יַחְדָּ֖יו נָפְל֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: This is the word that the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt: “Announce it in Egypt, and proclaim it in Migdol; proclaim it in Memphis and Tahpanhes: ‘Take your positions and prepare yourself, for the sword devours those around you.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet.
The LORD gave Jeremiah a message.
Nebuchadnezzar is the king of Babylon.
Nebuchadnezzar will come to attack the land of Egypt.
Announce this message in Egypt.
Proclaim it in Migdol.
Proclaim it in Memphis.
Proclaim it in Tahpanhes.
Say to the people: Take your positions.
Prepare yourselves.
The sword destroys those around you.
passages.original: הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל־ יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ הַנָּבִ֑יא לָב֗וֹא נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּר֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל לְהַכּ֖וֹת אֶת־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃ הַגִּ֤ידוּ בְמִצְרַ֙יִם֙ וְהַשְׁמִ֣יעוּ בְמִגְדּ֔וֹל וְהַשְׁמִ֥יעוּ בְנֹ֖ף וּבְתַחְפַּנְחֵ֑ס אִמְר֗וּ הִתְיַצֵּב֙ וְהָכֵ֣ן לָ֔ךְ כִּֽי־ אָכְלָ֥ה חֶ֖רֶב סְבִיבֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Why have your warriors been laid low? They cannot stand, for the LORD has thrust them down.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
\r\nThe LORD has great power.
\r\nThe LORD has spoken to Jeremiah the prophet.
\r\nThe LORD has sent a message about Egypt.
\r\nYour warriors have fallen.
\r\nYour warriors cannot stand.
\r\nThe LORD has pushed your warriors down.
passages.original: מַדּ֖וּעַ נִסְחַ֣ף אַבִּירֶ֑יךָ לֹ֣א עָמַ֔ד כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה הֲדָפֽוֹ׃

passages.text: They continue to stumble; indeed, they have fallen over one another. They say, ‘Get up! Let us return to our people and to the land of our birth, away from the sword of the oppressor.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet.
Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, will attack Egypt.
The Egyptian warriors stumble again and again.
They fall over one another.
The soldiers say, "Get up."
They say, "Let us return to our people."
They say, "Let us go back to the land where we were born."
They want to escape the sword of the oppressor.
passages.original: הִרְבָּ֖ה כּוֹשֵׁ֑ל גַּם־ נָפַ֞ל אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־ רֵעֵ֗הוּ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ ק֣וּמָה׀ וְנָשֻׁ֣בָה אֶל־ עַמֵּ֗נוּ וְאֶל־ אֶ֙רֶץ֙ מֽוֹלַדְתֵּ֔נוּ מִפְּנֵ֖י חֶ֥רֶב הַיּוֹנָֽה׃

passages.text: There they will cry out: ‘Pharaoh king of Egypt was all noise; he has let the appointed time pass him by.’
passages.sermon:
The people will cry out in that place.
They will speak about Pharaoh, the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh made much noise.
Pharaoh did not act when he should have.
Pharaoh missed the appointed time.
passages.original: קָרְא֖וּ שָׁ֑ם פַּרְעֹ֤ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ שָׁא֔וֹן הֶעֱבִ֖יר הַמּוֹעֵֽד׃

passages.text: As surely as I live, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts, there will come one who is like Tabor among the mountains and like Carmel by the sea.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the King.
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
The LORD of Hosts says, “As surely as I live, this is true.”
Someone will come.
This person will be strong and important.
He will stand out like Mount Tabor stands among the mountains.
He will be seen like Mount Carmel stands by the sea.
passages.original: חַי־ אָ֙נִי֙ נְאֻם־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמ֑וֹ כִּ֚י כְּתָב֣וֹר בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וּכְכַרְמֶ֖ל בַּיָּ֥ם יָבֽוֹא׃

passages.text: Pack your bags for exile, O daughter dwelling in Egypt! For Memphis will be laid waste, destroyed and uninhabited.
passages.sermon:
The people of Egypt live in the land.
God tells them to prepare for exile.
He calls them "daughter of Egypt."
God commands them to pack their belongings.
God warns them that Memphis will become a ruin.
No one will live in Memphis.
Memphis will be empty and destroyed.
passages.original: כְּלֵ֤י גוֹלָה֙ עֲשִׂ֣י לָ֔ךְ יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת־ מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּֽי־ נֹף֙ לְשַׁמָּ֣ה תִֽהְיֶ֔ה וְנִצְּתָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ין יוֹשֵֽׁב׃ס

passages.text: Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a gadfly from the north is coming against her.
passages.sermon: Egypt is like a beautiful young cow.\r\nA powerful enemy will come from the north.\r\nThis enemy will attack Egypt.
passages.original: עֶגְלָ֥ה יְפֵֽה־ פִיָּ֖ה מִצְרָ֑יִם קֶ֥רֶץ מִצָּפ֖וֹן בָּ֥א בָֽא׃

passages.text: Even the mercenaries among her are like fattened calves. They too will turn back; together they will flee, they will not stand their ground, for the day of calamity is coming upon them— the time of their punishment.
passages.sermon:
Egypt has mercenaries living among her.
These mercenaries are like fattened calves.
The mercenaries will turn back.
They will flee together.
They will not stand their ground.
A day of calamity is coming upon them.
This is the time of their punishment.
passages.original: גַּם־ שְׂכִרֶ֤יהָ בְקִרְבָּהּ֙ כְּעֶגְלֵ֣י מַרְבֵּ֔ק כִּֽי־ גַם־ הֵ֧מָּה הִפְנ֛וּ נָ֥סוּ יַחְדָּ֖יו לֹ֣א עָמָ֑דוּ כִּ֣י י֥וֹם אֵידָ֛ם בָּ֥א עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם עֵ֥ת פְּקֻדָּתָֽם׃

passages.text: Egypt will hiss like a fleeing serpent, for the enemy will advance in force; with axes they will come against her like woodsmen cutting down trees.
passages.sermon:
Egypt is a nation.
Egypt will make a sound like a snake that is fleeing.
The enemy will come against Egypt with great strength.
The enemy will carry axes.
The enemy will attack Egypt like men who cut down trees in a forest.
passages.original: קוֹלָ֖הּ כַּנָּחָ֣שׁ יֵלֵ֑ךְ כִּֽי־ בְחַ֣יִל יֵלֵ֔כוּ וּבְקַרְדֻּמּוֹת֙ בָּ֣אוּ לָ֔הּ כְּחֹטְבֵ֖י עֵצִֽים׃

passages.text: They will chop down her forest, declares the LORD, dense though it may be, for they are more numerous than locusts; they cannot be counted.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD says, "They will chop down her forest."
Her forest is very dense.
The people who come are more numerous than locusts.
No one can count them.
passages.original: כָּרְת֤וּ יַעְרָהּ֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֖י לֹ֣א יֵֽחָקֵ֑ר כִּ֤י רַבּוּ֙ מֵֽאַרְבֶּ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין לָהֶ֖ם מִסְפָּֽר׃

passages.text: The Daughter of Egypt will be put to shame; she will be delivered into the hands of the people of the north.”
passages.sermon:
Egypt is like a daughter.
She will feel shame.
God will give her to the people from the north.
The people from the north will take her.
passages.original: הֹבִ֖ישָׁה בַּת־ מִצְרָ֑יִם נִתְּנָ֖ה בְּיַ֥ד עַם־ צָפֽוֹן׃

passages.text: The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Behold, I am about to punish Amon god of Thebes, along with Pharaoh, Egypt with her gods and kings, and those who trust in Pharaoh.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is the God of Israel.
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
The LORD says, “I will punish Amon, the god of Thebes.
I will punish Pharaoh.
I will punish Egypt.
I will punish Egypt’s gods.
I will punish Egypt’s kings.
I will punish those who trust in Pharaoh.”
passages.original: אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הִנְנִ֤י פוֹקֵד֙ אֶל־ אָמ֣וֹן מִנֹּ֔א וְעַל־ פַּרְעֹה֙ וְעַל־ מִצְרַ֔יִם וְעַל־ אֱלֹהֶ֖יהָ וְעַל־ מְלָכֶ֑יהָ וְעַ֨ל־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה וְעַ֥ל הַבֹּטְחִ֖ים בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: I will deliver them into the hands of those who seek their lives—of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his officers. But after this, Egypt will be inhabited as in days of old, declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks these words.
The LORD will give Egypt and her leaders into the hands of their enemies.
These enemies seek their lives.
Nebuchadnezzar is king of Babylon.
The LORD will give Egypt and her leaders into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar.
The LORD will also give them into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar’s officers.
After this, Egypt will be inhabited again.
People will live in Egypt as they did in ancient times.
The LORD declares this.
passages.original: וּנְתַתִּ֗ים בְּיַד֙ מְבַקְשֵׁ֣י נַפְשָׁ֔ם וּבְיַ֛ד נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־ בָּבֶ֖ל וּבְיַד־ עֲבָדָ֑יו וְאַחֲרֵי־ כֵ֛ן תִּשְׁכֹּ֥ן כִּֽימֵי־ קֶ֖דֶם נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: But you, O Jacob My servant, do not be afraid, and do not be dismayed, O Israel. For I will surely save you out of a distant place, your descendants from the land of their captivity! Jacob will return to quiet and ease, with no one to make him afraid.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to Jacob, who is His servant.
Jacob is also called Israel.
The LORD tells Jacob not to be afraid.
The LORD tells Israel not to be dismayed.
The LORD promises to save Jacob from a faraway place.
The LORD will also save Jacob’s descendants from the land where they are captives.
Jacob will return to his land.
Jacob will live in peace and quiet.
No one will make Jacob afraid.
passages.original: וְ֠אַתָּה אַל־ תִּירָ֞א עַבְדִּ֤י יַֽעֲקֹב֙ וְאַל־ תֵּחַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֤י מוֹשִֽׁעֲךָ֙ מֵֽרָח֔וֹק וְאֶֽת־ זַרְעֲךָ֖ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ שִׁבְיָ֑ם וְשָׁ֧ב יַעֲק֛וֹב וְשָׁקַ֥ט וְשַׁאֲנַ֖ן וְאֵ֥ין מַחֲרִֽיד׃ס

passages.text: And you, My servant Jacob, do not be afraid, declares the LORD, for I am with you. Though I will completely destroy all the nations to which I have banished you, I will not completely destroy you. Yet I will discipline you justly, and will by no means leave you unpunished.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to Jacob, His servant.
Jacob is the ancestor of the people of Israel.
The LORD says, “Do not be afraid, Jacob.
I am with you.
I have sent you among many nations.
I will destroy all those nations completely.
But I will not destroy you completely.
I will discipline you with justice.
I will not leave you unpunished.”
passages.original: אַ֠תָּה אַל־ תִּירָ֞א עַבְדִּ֤י יַֽעֲקֹב֙ נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אִתְּךָ֖ אָ֑נִי כִּי֩ אֶעֱשֶׂ֨ה כָלָ֜ה בְּכָֽל־ הַגּוֹיִ֣ם׀ אֲשֶׁ֧ר הִדַּחְתִּ֣יךָ שָׁ֗מָּה וְאֹֽתְךָ֙ לֹא־ אֶעֱשֶׂ֣ה כָלָ֔ה וְיִסַּרְתִּ֙יךָ֙ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט וְנַקֵּ֖ה לֹ֥א אֲנַקֶּֽךָּ׃ס
